overview: Franco-Nevada is the largest gold-focused royalty and streaming company, holding the most diversified portfolio of cash-flow-producing royalty, stream and working interests in the industry (447 assets as of August 2026, including 121 producing). The Toronto-headquartered company does not operate mines or conduct exploration itself; instead it provides upfront capital to mine operators in exchange for a percentage of production or revenue, giving shareholders leveraged exposure to gold, silver and platinum group metals (plus a smaller diversified book of iron ore and oil/gas/NGL royalties) without taking on operating or capital cost risk. Shares are dual-listed as FNV on the TSX and NYSE, report in USD under IFRS, and the company is also the only major royalty/streaming name with direct exposure to the stalled Cobre Panamá copper-gold-silver mine.

business_model.summary: Franco-Nevada earns revenue by selling the metals/ounces it is entitled to under royalty and stream contracts; it collects cash with essentially no exposure to the underlying mine's operating or capital costs on 88-91% of revenue (royalties/streams), with the remainder from working interests, net profit interests, net royalty interests and gross margin royalties that are modestly cost-sensitive. In 2025, 88% of revenue came from mining assets (85% of that precious metals); energy (oil, gas, NGLs via a third-party marketing agent in the U.S. and Canada) made up the balance of the 'Diversified' segment alongside iron ore and other mining royalties. Reporting is denominated in Gold Equivalent Ounces (GEOs), which convert all commodity revenue (silver, PGMs, copper-linked streams, iron ore, oil & gas) into a gold-ounce-equivalent using fixed conversion ratios (starting 2026; previously variable market-price ratios) so investors can compare period-over-period volumes independent of price moves. 'Net GEOs' further nets out the smaller cost-bearing interests.

revenue_streams.name: Working interests / NPI / NRI / GMR (profit or cost-linked)

business_model.customer_type: No direct customers in the traditional sense; counterparties are mine/project operators (large diversified majors like Newmont, Barrick, Glencore, Lundin Mining, Sibanye-Stillwater, Rio Tinto down to junior developers) who deliver metal or make royalty payments. Capital recipients are B2B mining/energy companies seeking non-dilutive project financing.
business_model.geographic_mix: Highly diversified across the Americas (Chile, Peru, Mexico, Panama, Canada, U.S.), Africa (South Africa, Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire), Australia and other regions; largest single-asset exposures include Candelaria (Chile), Antapaccay/Antamina (Peru), Guadalupe-Palmarejo (Mexico), Côté Gold/Porcupine/Greenstone/Detour Lake/Musselwhite/Hemlo (Canada), and the Western Limb PGM stream (South Africa). Energy assets are concentrated in the U.S. (Haynesville, SCOOP/STACK, Permian) and Canadian Weyburn Unit.

competitive_position.market_position: Largest and most diversified royalty/streaming company by revenue and asset count; ranked #1 among gold-royalty peers by trailing revenue. More diversified across commodities (gold, silver, PGM, copper by-product exposure, iron ore, oil and gas) than Royal Gold (historically ~85% gold-weighted) or Wheaton Precious Metals (more silver-weighted, pure precious metals only, no energy).

moat_factors.description: The majority of interests (88-93% of revenue in recent years) are NSR royalties or streams, which pay out based on production/revenue with no deduction for operator cost inflation, capex overruns or operating losses -- a structural advantage over equity ownership of mines.

447 royalty/stream interests (121 producing) across multiple commodities, operators and geographies reduces single-asset/single-operator risk; small, stable corporate overhead (44 full-time employees) allows this large portfolio to be managed with minimal G&A drag.

Royalties/streams typically cover large land packages around a mine, giving free upside from exploration success by the operator (e.g., over 300 exploration/advanced-stage interests not reflected in guidance).

No debt drawn on revolver as of mid-2026, ~$4.3B of available capital (cash, equity investments, undrawn credit facilities), enabling FNV to act as a counter-cyclical financier when mining-sector capital is scarce and to win large, competitive deals (e.g., $1.05B Côté Gold royalty, $500M Western Limb PGM stream, $750M Cascabel financing).

moat_factors.factor: Reputation/track record as counterparty of choice
moat_factors.description: 18+ years of annual dividend increases and long-standing relationships with major operators (Barrick, Glencore, Newmont, Lundin Mining) support deal flow, though this is a softer advantage shared with Wheaton and Royal Gold.

weaknesses: No operational control: FNV cannot influence mine-plan decisions, cost management, or restart timing at underperforming or disrupted assets (starkly illustrated by Cobre Panamá)
Candelaria stream remains individually significant to total revenue, creating single-asset concentration risk despite overall diversification
Dependent on operators' accuracy/good faith in calculating and reporting production and payments, with limited audit rights
Reserve/production depletion requires continual redeployment of capital into new deals to sustain growth, making FNV a perpetual acquirer in a competitive bidding market

growth_drivers: Active and well-capitalized acquisition pipeline: over $1.7B deployed in 2025 alone (Western Limb PGM stream $500M, Côté Gold royalty $1.05B, Porcupine financing $300M+, Arthur Gold Project royalty $250M) plus further 2026 deals (i-80 Gold $250M royalty, Casa Berardi $100M stream, Bullabulling $120M, Victoria Gold portfolio)

Ramp-up of recently acquired/financed growth assets: Côté Gold, Porcupine, Valentine, Greenstone and Salares Norte are all ramping toward steady-state production, driving 2026 guidance of 510,000-570,000 GEOs (vs. 519,106 actual in 2025)

Possible Cobre Panamá stockpile processing and eventual restart: first copper concentrate produced in Q2 2026 from stockpile processing; ~70,000 tonnes of copper expected to be processed in 2026-2027, delivering ~23,100 gold ounces and 265,000 silver ounces to FNV; a full restart (not yet in guidance) could add an estimated 150,000-175,000 GEOs/year once ramped

Gold/silver/PGM price leverage: because royalty/stream revenue has no offsetting cost inflation, GEO-for-GEO revenue and margin expansion from higher metal prices flows almost entirely to the bottom line (FY2025 revenue +64% YoY largely on higher gold prices; H1 2026 revenue +67% YoY, a new half-year record)
Long-dated optionality portfolio: 300+ exploration/advanced-stage royalty and stream interests not included in guidance or the five-year outlook provide 'free' call options on future discoveries
Energy segment upside from elevated oil/gas prices (U.S. Haynesville, SCOOP/STACK, Permian; H1 2026 oil revenue +20% YoY) providing a secondary, uncorrelated growth lever
Continued dividend growth (19 consecutive annual increases through 2026, quarterly dividend raised 16% to $0.44/share) supporting the equity-income investor base

business.description: Mine has been on preservation and safe management (P&SM) with production halted since November 2023 following a Panama Supreme Court ruling against the concession; while stockpile processing resumed in 2026 (first concentrate produced Q2 2026, ~70,000 tonnes copper expected through 2027) and an environmental audit found 87.7% compliance, a full mine restart is not in guidance and remains contingent on Panamanian government policy, a ministerial commission review, and possible new concession terms.

Candelaria stream remains individually significant to total revenue; adverse developments at any single major asset (production stoppage, mine plan change, geotechnical event) can materially affect results.

FNV depends entirely on third-party operators for production decisions, cost management, exploration investment, and accurate royalty/stream payment calculations, with limited audit rights and no ability to compel production.

Long-term growth requires continually acquiring new royalties/streams in a competitive market against well-capitalized peers (Wheaton, Royal Gold, Triple Flag, Osisko, Sandstorm), potentially compressing future returns on new deals.

financial.description: Revenue and asset values are subject to currency fluctuations (CAD, AUD, BRL, MXN and others) even though FNV reports in USD; could affect realized margins and balance sheet carrying values.
Large, debt-light balance sheet model means future growth capital may come from equity issuance (including DRIP), which could dilute shareholders if deployed on less accretive deals.
Payments flow through operators; insolvency, lender restrictions, or payment delays by counterparties (especially smaller junior miners) can delay or impair cash flow.

regulatory.description: Cobre Panamá's future hinges on Panamanian government policy (presidential and ministerial decisions), a constitutionally compliant concession framework, and the outcome of a high-level ministerial commission; FNV and First Quantum both suspended related arbitration proceedings in 2025, reflecting a negotiated rather than litigated path forward with uncertain timing and terms.

FNV reached a September 2025 settlement with the Canada Revenue Agency resolving a multi-year transfer-pricing dispute (2013-2019) related to its Barbadian and Mexican subsidiaries at no incremental Canadian tax, but Canada enacted new transfer-pricing legislation effective 2026 that FNV is still evaluating; further CRA or other tax-authority reviews remain a recurring risk given FNV's offshore holding structure.

Underlying mine operators require environmental, indigenous-consultation, and mining permits across many countries (Peru, Chile, Mexico, South Africa, Canada, Australia, Ecuador); permitting delays or denials at any asset can delay expected production ramp-ups embedded in FNV's guidance.
Potential passive foreign investment company classification and possible future changes to Canadian tax treatment of offshore streams are specifically flagged as forward-looking risk factors.

macro.description: Revenue is directly tied to gold, silver, PGM, copper (via indexed streams), iron ore, oil and natural gas prices; gold pulled back over 20% from its January 2026 record high (~$5,400-5,600/oz) to roughly $4,180-4,270/oz by late September 2026 after its worst quarter since 2013 in Q2 2026, illustrating the two-way nature of this leverage even though FNV's 2026 guidance assumes a conservative $4,500/oz gold price.

Gold prices are influenced by real interest rates, Fed policy and USD strength; rate cuts have been a tailwind in 2025-2026 but any reversal (sustained higher-for-longer rates or USD strength) could pressure gold and silver prices and FNV's revenue.

Sudden macro or geopolitical shocks could impair operators' access to project financing, delaying development of FNV's advanced/exploration assets, and could also affect FNV's own liquidity and cost of capital.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold royalty/streaming remains a favored way to gain gold/precious-metals exposure with lower operating risk than equity ownership of miners; 2025-2026 saw record gold prices (peaking near $5,400-5,600/oz in January 2026) driven by central-bank buying, safe-haven demand and rate-cut expectations, before a sharp pullback (worst quarter since 2013 in Q2 2026) to roughly $4,100-4,300/oz by late Q3 2026. Silver and PGM markets have broadly tracked gold with added industrial-demand support. Energy royalty outlook is more mixed, with oil prices supported by geopolitical disruption (Iran-related conflict) while natural gas prices softened on ample supply.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - FNV's royalty/stream structure smooths much of the operating-cost cyclicality miners face, but revenue still swings directly with commodity prices and production volumes; FY2023 posted a net loss largely tied to the Cobre Panamá-related impairment following the mine's shutdown, showing downside is not fully insulated.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High indirect sensitivity via gold price (non-yielding asset competes with real rates) and discount-rate effects on asset valuations; low direct balance-sheet sensitivity given FNV carries no net debt.

recent_developments.event: Record H1 2026 results: revenue of $1,231.6M (+67% YoY), net income of $822.6M (+80% YoY, $4.27/share), Adjusted EBITDA of $1,121.6M (+63% YoY); Q2 2026 revenue $580.9M (+57% YoY), net income $354.0M (+43% YoY)

Cobre Panamá transitioned to active stockpile processing under the approved P&SM Processing Program: first processing train commissioned May 2026, first copper concentrate produced, ~2.1 million tonnes processed in the quarter producing 3,216 tonnes of copper; First Quantum guided 30,000-40,000 tonnes of copper from Cobre Panamá in 2026 (70,000 tonnes total through 2027), with FNV stream deliveries (~23,100 gold oz, ~265,000 silver oz) expected to begin Q3 2026

Panama's MiAmbiente published SGS's integral environmental/social/legal/fiscal audit of Cobre Panamá confirming 87.7% compliance (361 of 370 commitments fulfilled); GOP established a high-level ministerial commission to evaluate the mine's future

Multiple new royalty/stream acquisitions closed: i-80 Gold Royalty ($250M, closed March 2026), Casa Berardi Stream with Orezone ($100M, closed March 2026), Bullabulling Royalty with Minerals 260 ($120M, closed Feb/March 2026), Victoria Gold Corp. royalty portfolio ($40M, closed April 2026), plus smaller Australian royalties (Youanmi, Comet Vale, Greenstone top-up)

SolGold (Cascabel project, Ecuador) acquired by Jiangxi Copper; JCC exercised buy-back option for 50% of FNV's Cascabel stream and NSR, delivering $40.7M of gold ounces plus $97.5M cash to FNV and recognizing a $63.8M gain in Q1 2026 net income
Quarterly dividend raised 16% to $0.44/share, the 19th consecutive annual dividend increase, effective for full-year 2026

Settled multi-year CRA transfer-pricing dispute (2013-2019 tax years, Barbadian/Mexican subsidiaries) with no incremental Canadian tax owed; related security deposits/letters of credit subsequently released
Acquired Côté Gold mine royalty (7.5% gross margin royalty) from a private third party for $1.05 billion, one of FNV's largest-ever single royalty acquisitions
Closed $500M Western Limb precious metals (gold + platinum) stream on Sibanye-Stillwater's Marikana/Rustenburg/Kroondal South African PGM operations

First Quantum and FNV each agreed to suspend their respective international arbitration proceedings against the Government of Panama, signaling a negotiated path toward resolving Cobre Panamá's status

guidance.as_of: Q2 2026 MD&A (filed August 11, 2026); 2026 guidance originally issued March 10, 2026 in FY2025 MD&A/AIF

items.notes: H1 2026 actual was 268,758 GEOs (+13% YoY); company says it is 'tracking towards the upper half' of the range given Cobre Panamá stockpile deliveries beginning Q3 2026 and H2-weighted production at Candelaria, Tocantinzinho, Côté Gold, Greenstone and Valentine. Does not include any full Cobre Panamá restart or further Continental Royalty Acquisition Venture contributions.
H1 2026 actual 182,382 oz, roughly on pace at the midpoint.
H1 2026 actual $164.8M; management notes elevated oil prices (H1 oil revenue +20% YoY) could push toward the upper end -- each $10/bbl increase above the $70 WTI assumption adds ~12% to oil revenue.
H1 2026 actual $161.9M, in line with guidance.
Company is still evaluating the impact of new Canadian transfer-pricing legislation enacted March 26, 2026, effective 2026 onward.
Excludes any Cobre Panamá contribution; a restart could add a potential 150,000-175,000 GEOs/year once the mine ramps to full capacity, which is not currently modeled.

items.target: $4,500/oz Au, $75.00/oz Ag, $2,000/oz Pt, $1,650/oz Pd, $100/tonne Fe (62% CFR China), $70/bbl WTI, $3.00/mcf Henry Hub
items.notes: Starting 2026, FNV adopted fixed GEO conversion ratios at these assumed prices (replacing the prior variable, market-price-based conversion), intended to make reported GEOs better reflect underlying production volumes rather than price swings.

guidance.management_commentary: Management highlighted 2026 as benefiting from a first full year of contribution from Côté Gold, Porcupine and Valentine, continued ramp-up at Salares Norte and Greenstone, and the start of Cobre Panamá stockpile-ore deliveries (not previously in guidance). CFO/MD&A commentary flagged that elevated oil prices and the Cobre Panamá stockpile program both represent upside optionality versus the base guidance range. On Cobre Panamá specifically, management reiterated hope for a negotiated resolution with the Panamanian government but gave no restart timeline, noting the government's ministerial commission is still evaluating the mine's future following the completed environmental audit.

bull_case: Pure-play, cost-insulated leverage to gold/silver/PGM prices through a royalty/stream model with no operating or capital cost exposure on ~90% of revenue, delivering record H1 2026 revenue (+67% YoY) and EBITDA margins above 90%

Deep, well-capitalized acquisition pipeline ($4.3B available capital as of mid-2026) continuing to add new royalties/streams at scale ($1.05B Côté Gold, $500M Western Limb, $250M i-80 Gold, among many others in 2025-2026), growing the asset base faster than depletion

Multiple existing growth assets (Côté Gold, Porcupine, Valentine, Greenstone, Salares Norte) are still ramping toward steady-state production, providing visible organic GEO growth even before any further acquisitions

Cobre Panamá optionality is a free call option not in guidance: stockpile processing has already resumed (first concentrate in Q2 2026) and a full restart, if ultimately negotiated with Panama, could add 150,000-175,000 GEOs annually -- a material (~25-30%) increase versus current guided levels

19 consecutive years of dividend increases (raised 16% to $0.44/quarter for 2026) backed by a debt-free balance sheet, appealing to income-oriented and lower-risk gold investors relative to equity miners
bear_case: Cobre Panamá's full restart remains hostage to Panamanian domestic politics and legal/constitutional constraints on the concession; resolution timing and ultimate economics (new royalty/tax terms) are highly uncertain, and the prior shutdown already drove a large net loss in FY2023

Gold has already pulled back more than 20% from its January 2026 record high after its worst quarter since 2013 in Q2 2026, illustrating that FNV's revenue (and the premium valuation the market assigns to royalty companies) is directly exposed to a sustained commodity price correction

FNV's growth model depends on continually winning new royalty/stream deals in a competitive market against well-funded peers (Wheaton, Royal Gold, Triple Flag, Sandstorm, Osisko), raising the risk that future acquisitions are priced less attractively as the best assets get bid away

No operational control over any underlying mine: production stoppages, mine-plan changes, geotechnical events, or operator financial distress at any single material asset (e.g., Candelaria) can directly and unpredictably hit FNV's reported results

Royalty/streaming companies like FNV typically trade at a premium multiple to gold-price-adjusted NAV versus producers; if that premium compresses (e.g., on rate hikes, a stronger USD, or a prolonged gold bear market) the stock could underperform even if underlying metal prices are merely flat
